query: Is (P AND NOT P) a contradiction?
reasoning:
1. Recall: a statement that is false under every possible truth assignment is called a contradiction.
2. Recall: for any P, when P is true, NOT P is false; when P is false, NOT P is true — so P and NOT P always have opposite truth values.
3. Recall: an AND statement is true only when both parts are true; since P and NOT P (from step 2) can never both be true, (P AND NOT P) is false in every case.
4. Compare: a statement false in every case (step 3) matches the definition of a contradiction (step 1) → yes.
